records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל עַד־מָתַי֙ אַתָּה֙ מִתְאַבֵּ֣ל אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַאֲנִ֣י מְאַסְתִּ֔יו מִמְּלֹ֖ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מַלֵּ֨א קַרְנְךָ֜ שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֵ֤ךְ אֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֙ אֶל־יִשַׁ֣י בֵּֽית־הַלַּחְמִ֔י כִּֽי־רָאִ֧יתִי בְּבָנָ֛יו לִ֖י מֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Samuel, Until when [are] you mourning for Saul, and I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn [with] oil and go; I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen among his sons for myself a king.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "How long will you go on mourning for Saul, now that I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and set out. I am sending you to Jesse in Bethlehem, because I have chosen one of his sons to be king for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "How long [are] you mourning for Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn [with] oil and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} a king among his sons."

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "How long will you keep on being sad about Saul? I have rejected him. He will not be king over Israel. Fill your horn with olive oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I have chosen one of his sons to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} king."

decisions.choice: mourning for Saul whom the LORD has rejected
decisions.reason: The chapter follows straight on from 15:35, where Samuel mourned for Saul and Yahweh regretted making him king. The verb "rejected" is the word of 15:23 and 15:26: Saul rejected Yahweh's word, so Yahweh rejected him as king. Samuel's grief is real, but the time for it is over.

decisions.choice: fill your horn with oil: prepare to anoint a king
decisions.reason: Oil was carried in an animal's horn. Pouring oil on someone's head set that person apart for an office; Samuel had anointed Saul with oil from a flask (10:1). The command already tells Samuel what the journey is for.

decisions.choice: I have seen for myself a king: I have chosen and provided a king
alternatives: I have provided for myself a king
decisions.reason: "See" here means to look out and select, as in Genesis 22:8, 14, where God "sees" (provides) the lamb. "For myself" stands against the story of Saul, the king the people asked for (8:5; 12:13). This king is Yahweh's own choice.

decisions.choice: Jesse the Bethlehemite: Jesse from Bethlehem in Judah
decisions.reason: Bethlehem lay a few miles south of Jerusalem, in the hill country of Judah. Jesse was the grandson of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17-22).

decisions.choice: chosen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "chosen" for "seen" in this sense of picking out (m3); Literal keeps "seen".

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: Readable names the kind of oil used for anointing (Exodus 30:24) and splits the rejection into short sentences.

records.heading: Samuel anoints David

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֵ֣יךְ אֵלֵ֔ךְ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שָׁא֖וּל וַהֲרָגָ֑נִיסוַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה עֶגְלַ֤ת בָּקָר֙ תִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ לִזְבֹּ֥חַ לַֽיהוָ֖ה בָּֽאתִי׃
records.gloss: And said Samuel, How will I go? And will hear Saul and he will kill me. And said Yahweh, A heifer of [the] herd you will take in your hand, and you will say, To sacrifice to Yahweh I have come.
pieces: Samuel said, "How can I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me." {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Take a young cow with you and say, 'I have come to offer a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

L.2: And Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears, he will kill me." And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Take a heifer of the herd in your hand, and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

R.2: Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears about it, he will kill me." {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Take a young cow with you. Say, 'I have come to offer a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

decisions.choice: Samuel fears for his life
decisions.reason: To anoint another king while Saul still reigned was treason in Saul's eyes. Saul had already shown that he could turn on those close to him (14:44), and Samuel had just announced that his kingdom was torn from him (15:28).

decisions.choice: say, I have come to sacrifice: a true reason given, the full purpose kept hidden
decisions.reason: The sacrifice is real; Samuel holds it (verse 5). Yahweh does not tell him to say anything false, but he does not have to tell everyone why he has come. The hidden purpose protects Samuel and David from Saul.

decisions.choice: in your hand: with you
decisions.reason: "Take in your hand" means to take along with you; a heifer is led, not carried.

decisions.choice: a young cow
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "young cow" for a heifer, a cow that has not yet borne a calf; Literal keeps "heifer of the herd".

decisions.choice: the quotation stays open
decisions.reason: Yahweh's words go on into verse 3, so the quotation mark closes there.

records.source: וְקָרָ֥אתָ לְיִשַׁ֖י בַּזָּ֑בַח וְאָֽנֹכִ֗י אוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶֽׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וּמָשַׁחְתָּ֣ לִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַ֖ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you will do, and you will anoint for me [the one] whom I say to you.
pieces: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what to do. You will anoint for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the one I name to you."

L.3: And you shall invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do, and you shall anoint for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [the one] whom I say to you."

R.3: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice. Then I will show you what to do. You will pour oil on the one I point out to you. That will show that I have chosen him."

decisions.choice: I will make known: Yahweh keeps the choice in his own hands
decisions.reason: Samuel is not told the name in advance. He must wait for Yahweh to show him, step by step, which son to anoint (verses 6-12).

decisions.choice: anoint for me: anoint as my king
decisions.reason: "For me" picks up "for myself" in verse 1. The one Samuel anoints will be Yahweh's king.

decisions.choice: pour oil on ... That will show that I have chosen him
decisions.reason: Readable explains what anointing is and what it meant here (verse 1, m2; verse 13).

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם וַיֶּחֶרְד֞וּ זִקְנֵ֤י הָעִיר֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֹ֥ם בּוֹאֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And did Samuel what spoke Yahweh, and he came [to] Bethlehem; and trembled [the] elders of the city to meet him, and he said, [Is it] peace, your coming?
pieces: Samuel did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said and went to Bethlehem. The elders of the town came out trembling to meet him and asked, "Have you come in peace?"

L.4: And Samuel did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city came trembling to meet him, and said, "Is your coming peace?"

R.4: Samuel did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told him and went to Bethlehem. The leaders of the town were afraid when they came to meet him. They asked, "Have you come as a friend?"

decisions.choice: the elders trembled: a visit from the prophet could mean judgment
decisions.reason: Samuel went around Israel as judge (7:15-17), and he had just put Agag to death (15:33). A sudden visit from him could mean that the town had done wrong or that trouble was coming. The elders were the town's leading men, the heads of its families.

decisions.choice: is your coming peace: do you come with good intent
decisions.reason: Shalom here means well-being and friendship, the opposite of trouble. The same question is asked when a visitor's purpose is unknown (1 Kings 2:13; 2 Kings 9:17-22).

decisions.choice: and he said: one spoke for the elders
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. Either one elder spoke for all, or the writer treats the elders as one group.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for the elders, since the point is their position in the town, not their age.

decisions.choice: as a friend
decisions.reason: Readable puts "in peace" in plain words (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀שָׁל֗וֹם לִזְבֹּ֤חַ לַֽיהוָה֙ בָּ֔אתִי הִֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וּבָאתֶ֥ם אִתִּ֖י בַּזָּ֑בַח וַיְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֶת־יִשַׁי֙ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֔יו וַיִּקְרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ם לַזָּֽבַח׃
records.gloss: And he said, Peace; to sacrifice to Yahweh I have come. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice. And he consecrated Jesse and his sons, and he invited them to the sacrifice.
pieces: He said, "In peace. I have come to offer a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Make yourselves holy and come with me to the sacrifice." He made Jesse and his sons holy and invited them to the sacrifice.

L.5: And he said, "Peace. I have come to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." And he consecrated Jesse and his sons, and invited them to the sacrifice.

R.5: Samuel answered, "Yes, I come in peace. I have come to offer a sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Get yourselves ready and make yourselves clean, and then come with me to the sacrifice." Samuel also helped Jesse and his sons to get ready, and he invited them to the sacrifice.

decisions.choice: consecrate: make ready to come near to God
decisions.reason: Before a sacrifice or a meeting with God, people made themselves holy by washing, putting on clean clothes and keeping away from what made them unclean (Exodus 19:10-15; Joshua 3:5). Samuel himself oversees this for Jesse's family.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice: an offering followed by a shared meal
decisions.reason: Part of such a sacrifice was eaten by the guests at a feast, as at Samuel's sacrifice in 9:12-13, 22-24. Verse 11 speaks of not sitting down until David comes.

decisions.choice: make yourselves holy
decisions.reason: Balanced says "make holy" for "consecrate", the plainer word for setting someone apart for God.

decisions.choice: get yourselves ready and make yourselves clean
decisions.reason: Readable describes what consecrating oneself meant (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֔ם וַיַּ֖רְא אֶת־אֱלִיאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַ֛ךְ נֶ֥גֶד יְהוָ֖ה מְשִׁיחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, in their coming, and he saw Eliab, and he said, Surely before Yahweh [is] his anointed.
pieces: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, "Surely here before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stands {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed!"

L.6: And it happened when they came, he saw Eliab and said, "Surely before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed."

R.6: When they came, Samuel saw Eliab, Jesse's oldest son. He thought, "This must be the man {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen to be king. Here he is, standing in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: he said: he said to himself
decisions.reason: "Said" often means said in one's own mind (Genesis 17:17; 1 Samuel 18:17). Yahweh's answer in verse 7 replies to what Samuel thought.

decisions.choice: his anointed: the king Yahweh has chosen
decisions.reason: "Anointed" is the title of the king set apart by Yahweh (2:10; 12:3; 24:7). Samuel takes Eliab to be the one he has come to anoint.

decisions.choice: Eliab: Jesse's firstborn, tall like Saul
decisions.reason: Eliab was Jesse's oldest son (17:13). Verse 7 shows that Samuel was struck by his height, just as the people had been struck by Saul, a head taller than everyone (9:2; 10:23-24).

decisions.choice: thought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "thought" so that readers do not take it that Samuel spoke aloud (m1).

decisions.choice: Jesse's oldest son ... the man the LORD has chosen to be king
decisions.reason: Readable adds who Eliab was (17:13) and explains "his anointed" (m2), as the book's terms do for "the LORD's anointed".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אַל־תַּבֵּ֧ט אֶל־מַרְאֵ֛הוּ וְאֶל־גְּבֹ֥הַּ קוֹמָת֖וֹ כִּ֣י מְאַסְתִּ֑יהוּ כִּ֣י׀לֹ֗א אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִרְאֶה֙ הָאָדָ֔ם כִּ֤י הָֽאָדָם֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה לַעֵינַ֔יִם וַיהוָ֖ה יִרְאֶ֥ה לַלֵּבָֽב׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Samuel, Do not look to his appearance and to [the] height of his stature, for I have rejected him; for not what sees the man; for the man sees to the eyes, and Yahweh sees to the heart.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Pay no attention to his looks or to how tall he is, because I have rejected him. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does not see in the way {{gender:a person|man}} sees. {{gender:A person|Man}} looks at what is there for the eyes, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looks at the heart."

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For [it is] not what {{gender:a human being|man}} sees, for {{gender:a human being|man}} sees to the eyes, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sees to the heart."

R.7: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Do not think about how fine he looks or how tall he is. I have not chosen him. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does not see things the way people do. People see what is on the outside, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sees what is inside a person."

decisions.choice: his appearance and his height: the very things that marked Saul
decisions.reason: Saul had been chosen by a people who admired his looks and height (9:2; 10:23-24). Yahweh warns Samuel not to judge the same way again. "Rejected" is the word used of Saul himself (verse 1; 15:23, 26).

decisions.choice: for not what man sees: Yahweh does not see as a human being sees
alternatives: for it is not as man sees
decisions.reason: The wording is very short, "for not what man sees", and leaves the hearer to supply "does Yahweh see". The ancient Septuagint translation fills this out: God does not look as a human being looks. The rest of the verse makes the sense clear.

decisions.choice: sees to the eyes: looks at what the eyes can take in
decisions.reason: "To the eyes" means what is open to view: looks, size, bearing. The phrase may also mean that a person looks no further than the eyes can reach.

decisions.choice: Yahweh sees to the heart: he judges the inner person
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the inner life: thought, will, desire and loyalty. Samuel had told Saul that Yahweh sought "a man after his own heart" (13:14). Yahweh's choice rests on what a person is within, which only he can see (16:12 notes that David was handsome too, but that is not why he is chosen; 1 Kings 8:39; Jeremiah 17:10).

decisions.choice: the man: human beings in general
decisions.reason: The word here is the general word for a human being, set against Yahweh. Women and men alike are meant.

decisions.choice: a human being / a person (alternative: man)
decisions.reason: The inclusive form is the default because the word means any human being (m5); the gender setting gives the traditional "man". Readable's "people" is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: The LORD does not see in the way a person sees
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the words the Hebrew leaves the hearer to add (m2).

decisions.choice: I have not chosen him
decisions.reason: Readable puts "I have rejected him" positively: Eliab is not the one Yahweh has chosen. It also says "inside a person" for "the heart" (m4).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֤א יִשַׁי֙ אֶל־אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר גַּם־בָּזֶ֖ה לֹֽא־בָחַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And called Jesse Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel, and he said, Also this [one] not has chosen Yahweh.
pieces: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him walk past Samuel. But Samuel said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen this one either."

L.8: And Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen this one either."

R.8: Then Jesse called his son Abinadab and had him walk in front of Samuel. But Samuel said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen this one either."

decisions.choice: made him pass before Samuel: presented him for Samuel to look at
decisions.reason: Each son is brought in turn past the prophet, who waits for Yahweh to show him the one (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Abinadab: Jesse's second son
decisions.reason: Abinadab is the second son, after Eliab (17:13; 1 Chronicles 2:13).

decisions.choice: his son
decisions.reason: Readable says that Abinadab is Jesse's son.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר יִשַׁ֖י שַׁמָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר גַּם־בָּזֶ֖ה לֹא־בָחַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And made pass Jesse Shammah, and he said, Also this [one] not has chosen Yahweh.
pieces: Next Jesse had Shammah walk past. But Samuel said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen this one either."

L.9: And Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen this one either."

R.9: Next Jesse had Shammah walk past. But Samuel said again, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen this one either."

decisions.choice: Shammah: Jesse's third son
decisions.reason: He is the third son (17:13). Elsewhere his name appears as Shimea or Shimeah (2 Samuel 13:3; 1 Chronicles 2:13), forms of the same name.

decisions.choice: the same words as verse 8
decisions.reason: The answer is repeated word for word; the story slows down to show son after son passing by.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר יִשַׁ֛י שִׁבְעַ֥ת בָּנָ֖יו לִפְנֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־יִשַׁ֔י לֹא־בָחַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בָּאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And made pass Jesse seven of his sons before Samuel, and said Samuel to Jesse, Not has chosen Yahweh these.
pieces: Jesse had seven of his sons walk past Samuel, but Samuel said to Jesse, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen any of these."

L.10: And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen these."

R.10: In this way Jesse had seven of his sons walk past Samuel. But Samuel told Jesse, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not chosen any of these."

decisions.choice: seven of his sons: all the sons present, Eliab and the others
decisions.reason: Verses 6-9 name the first three; this verse sums up the whole line. Seven sons are present and one is missing, for Jesse had eight sons (17:12). 1 Chronicles 2:13-15 lists only seven, with David as the seventh; one son may have died without children.

decisions.choice: seven: a full number, yet not the one
decisions.reason: Seven is often the number of completeness. Seven sons would seem a full family, yet Yahweh's choice is outside it.

decisions.choice: any of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "any of" to make clear that none of the seven is chosen.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל אֶל־יִשַׁי֮ הֲתַ֣מּוּ הַנְּעָרִים֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר ע֚וֹד שָׁאַ֣ר הַקָּטָ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֥ה רֹעֶ֖ה בַּצֹּ֑אן וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל אֶל־יִשַׁי֙ שִׁלְחָ֣ה וְקָחֶ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־נָסֹ֖ב עַד־בֹּא֥וֹ פֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Samuel to Jesse, Are finished the young men? And he said, Still remains the small [one], and there, he [is] shepherding with the flock. And said Samuel to Jesse, Send and bring him, for not we will go around until his coming here.
pieces: Then Samuel asked Jesse, "Are these all the boys you have?" Jesse answered, "There is still the youngest. He is out looking after the sheep." Samuel said to Jesse, "Send for him and bring him here. We will not sit down to eat until he comes."

L.11: And Samuel said to Jesse, "Are the young men finished?" And he said, "There still remains the youngest, and look, he is shepherding the flock." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and bring him, for we will not go around until he comes here."

R.11: Then Samuel asked Jesse, "Are these all the sons you have?" Jesse answered, "There is still the youngest one, but he is out in the fields taking care of the sheep." Samuel said, "Send someone to bring him. We will not sit down to the feast until he gets here."

decisions.choice: the small one: the youngest, and also the least
decisions.reason: The word means both "youngest" and "small". After verse 7 the reader hears both: the son no one thought to call is the smallest in his family's eyes, the opposite of tall Eliab. Saul too once called himself the least (9:21).

decisions.choice: shepherding the flock: the work of the least important son
decisions.reason: Watching the sheep was left to the youngest. Jesse did not think him worth calling. Shepherd was also a picture of a king (2 Samuel 5:2; Psalm 78:70-72).

decisions.choice: we will not go around: we will not sit down to the meal
alternatives: we will not go around the altar
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn or go around. It may mean taking places around the table for the sacrificial meal (verse 5), or going around the altar, or turning away to leave. Each way, nothing goes forward until the youngest comes.

decisions.choice: the young men: Jesse's sons
decisions.reason: The word is used of boys and young men; here it means the sons who passed by.

decisions.choice: sit down to eat / sit down to the feast
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the likeliest sense (m3); Literal keeps "go around".

decisions.choice: out in the fields
decisions.reason: Readable says where the sheep were kept.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח וַיְבִיאֵ֨הוּ֙ וְה֣וּא אַדְמוֹנִ֔י עִם־יְפֵ֥ה עֵינַ֖יִם וְט֣וֹב רֹ֑אִיפוַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה ק֥וּם מְשָׁחֵ֖הוּ כִּֽי־זֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And he sent and brought him, and he [was] ruddy, with beautiful eyes and good of appearance. And said Yahweh, Arise, anoint him, for this [is] he.
pieces: So Jesse sent for him and had him brought in. He had a healthy, glowing look, with fine eyes, and he was handsome. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Get up and anoint him. He is the one."

L.12: And he sent and brought him in. And he [was] ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good in appearance. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Arise, anoint him, for this [is] he."

R.12: So Jesse sent for him and brought him in. His skin glowed with health, he had beautiful eyes, and he was good-looking. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Get up and pour the oil on him. He is the one."

decisions.choice: ruddy: reddish in color
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root for "red" and is also used of Esau at birth (Genesis 25:25). It may describe a fresh, reddish complexion or reddish hair. It is said again of David in 17:42.

decisions.choice: David is handsome too, but that is not why he is chosen
decisions.reason: After verse 7 the writer notes David's good looks without making them the reason for Yahweh's choice. Yahweh has seen his heart; the looks are given as a matter of fact.

decisions.choice: this is he: the one Yahweh had promised to show
decisions.reason: Yahweh now does what he said in verse 3: he names the one Samuel is to anoint.

decisions.choice: a healthy, glowing look / his skin glowed with health
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the sense of a fresh, reddish complexion (m1) rather than the rare English word "ruddy", which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: pour the oil on him
decisions.reason: Readable says what "anoint" means, as in verse 3, and says whom Yahweh spoke to.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶת־קֶ֣רֶן הַשֶּׁ֗מֶן וַיִּמְשַׁ֣ח אֹתוֹ֮ בְּקֶ֣רֶב אֶחָיו֒ וַתִּצְלַ֤ח רֽוּחַ־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיָּ֣קָם שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הָרָמָֽתָה׃ס
records.gloss: And took Samuel [the] horn of the oil and anointed him in [the] midst of his brothers, and rushed [the] Spirit of Yahweh on David from the day the that and onward. And arose Samuel and went [to] Ramah.
pieces: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him there among his brothers, and the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rushed on David from that day on. Then Samuel set out and went back to Ramah.

L.13: And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rushed on David from that day and onward. And Samuel arose and went to Ramah.

R.13: So Samuel took the horn of oil and poured it on David's head while his brothers watched. From that day on, the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on David with power. Then Samuel left and went home to Ramah.

decisions.choice: David: the name is given only now
decisions.reason: Through the whole scene the youngest son has had no name. The writer names him for the first time at the moment the Spirit comes on him. From here on, the story of the books of Samuel is the story of David.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Yahweh rushed on David: came on him with power
decisions.reason: The verb means to rush in or break through. It is used of the Spirit coming on Samson (Judges 14:6, 19; 15:14) and on Saul (10:6, 10; 11:6). With Saul and Samson it came at certain moments; here it stays with David "from that day and onward".

decisions.choice: in the midst of his brothers: with his brothers present
decisions.reason: The anointing takes place in front of the family. Nothing is said of what they understood; Eliab's anger in 17:28 suggests he did not accept it.

decisions.choice: Ramah: Samuel's home town
decisions.reason: Ramah, in the hill country of Ephraim, was Samuel's home (1:19; 7:17; 15:34).

decisions.choice: poured it on David's head while his brothers watched
decisions.reason: Readable explains anointing and "in the midst of his brothers" (m3), and names David as the one anointed.

decisions.choice: came on David with power
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "rushed on" means (m2); Literal and Balanced keep "rushed on", as Judges 14:6 does.

records.source: וְר֧וּחַ יְהוָ֛ה סָ֖רָה מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֑וּל וּבִֽעֲתַ֥תּוּ רֽוּחַ־רָעָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] Spirit of Yahweh turned aside from with Saul, and terrified him a spirit of evil from with Yahweh.
pieces: Now the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left Saul, and an evil spirit from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tormented him.

L.14: And the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned away from Saul, and an evil spirit from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} terrified him.

R.14: But the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left Saul. Instead, an evil spirit sent from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled him with terror.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Yahweh left Saul: the gift that made him king was taken away
decisions.reason: The Spirit that rushed on Saul at the start of his reign (10:6, 10; 11:6) now leaves him, just as it comes on David (verse 13). The two verses are set side by side: one king rises as the other falls. Saul is still on the throne, but Yahweh's power is no longer with him (18:12; 28:15).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit: a spirit that brings harm and distress
decisions.reason: The word ra'ah can mean moral evil, but also harm, trouble or disaster (Amos 3:6; Isaiah 45:7), as with the spirit sent between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem (Judges 9:23). What the spirit does to Saul is to fill him with dread and darkness of mind, and later rage (18:10-11; 19:9-10). Whether a spirit-being is meant or a troubled state of mind sent on him, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: from Yahweh: God acts in judgment on a king he has rejected
decisions.reason: The spirit comes "from Yahweh". Saul had rejected Yahweh's word, and Yahweh had rejected him (15:23, 26). Scripture speaks the same way of God sending an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem (Judges 9:23) and a deceiving spirit to judge Ahab (1 Kings 22:19-23). Nothing happens outside Yahweh's rule, and he uses even harm to judge; but he remains the righteous judge, not the author of Saul's sin. The spirit later moves Saul to violence (18:10-11), yet the guilt for it stays with Saul.

decisions.choice: terrified him: seized him with sudden fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to fall on someone with terror, to frighten suddenly. It is used of terrors that overwhelm a person (2 Samuel 22:5; Job 3:5), and it returns in verse 15.

decisions.choice: tormented
decisions.reason: Balanced says "tormented" for the spirit's repeated attacks of terror (verses 15, 23); Literal keeps "terrified" and Readable "filled him with terror".

decisions.choice: sent from
decisions.reason: Readable says "sent from the LORD" to make clear that the spirit came from Yahweh and was under his rule (m3), as "God sent" in Judges 9:23.

records.heading: David plays the lyre for Saul

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־שָׁא֖וּל אֵלָ֑יו הִנֵּה־נָ֧א רֽוּחַ־אֱלֹהִ֛ים רָעָ֖ה מְבַעִתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said [the] servants of Saul to him, Look, please, a spirit of God, evil, [is] terrifying you.
pieces: Saul's officials said to him, "You can see that an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.

L.15: And Saul's servants said to him, "Look now, an evil spirit of God is terrifying you.

R.15: Saul's officials said to him, "An evil spirit from God is filling you with terror.

decisions.choice: an evil spirit of God: an evil spirit sent by God
decisions.reason: "Of God" names where the spirit comes from: it is the spirit "from Yahweh" of verse 14. The servants use the general word for God, as people speaking in ordinary life often do.

decisions.choice: look now: a polite opening
decisions.reason: The servants point to what everyone can see before making their suggestion (verse 16). Their words run on into the next verse.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable call Saul's servants "officials", as with the king's servants elsewhere in these books; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: from God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "from God" for "of God" (m1).

records.source: יֹאמַר־נָ֤א אֲדֹנֵ֨נוּ֙ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ יְבַקְשׁ֕וּ אִ֕ישׁ יֹדֵ֖עַ מְנַגֵּ֣ן בַּכִּנּ֑וֹר וְהָיָ֗ה בִּֽהְי֨וֹת עָלֶ֤יךָ רֽוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים֙ רָעָ֔ה וְנִגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ וְט֥וֹב לָֽךְ׃פ
records.gloss: Let say, please, our lord; your servants [are] before you; let them seek a man knowing playing on the lyre, and it will be, when is on you a spirit of God, evil, and he will play with his hand, and good [it will be] for you.
pieces: Let our lord give the order to your servants here before you, and they will look for a man who knows how to play the lyre. Then, whenever the evil spirit from God comes on you, he will play and you will feel better."

L.16: Let our lord now speak. Your servants [are] before you. Let them seek a man who knows how to play the lyre. And it will be, when an evil spirit of God is on you, he will play with his hand, and it will be good for you."

R.16: Our master, just give the order to us, your servants. We will look for a man who can play the lyre well. When the evil spirit from God comes on you, he will play music for you, and you will feel better."

decisions.choice: the lyre: a stringed instrument held in the hands
decisions.reason: The kinnor had a wooden frame and strings and was played by hand, by plucking or with a pick. It was played at feasts and in worship (Genesis 4:21; 1 Samuel 10:5).

decisions.choice: music to ease the troubled spirit
decisions.reason: Music was known to calm and lift the mind. The servants hope that skilled playing will bring Saul relief when the spirit comes on him, and verse 23 shows that it did.

decisions.choice: your servants before you: a polite way of saying "we"
decisions.reason: The servants speak of themselves in the third person, as people did when speaking to a king.

decisions.choice: knowing: skilled
decisions.reason: "Knowing how to play" means being able to play well, as verse 17 says.

decisions.choice: your servants
decisions.reason: When the speakers call themselves "your servants" before the king, Balanced and Readable keep "servants", the humble form of address.

decisions.choice: you will feel better
decisions.reason: "It will be good for you" is put as "you will feel better".

decisions.choice: Our master
decisions.reason: Readable says "master" for "our lord", the king; it is not a title of God here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־עֲבָדָ֑יו רְאוּ־נָ֣א לִ֗י אִ֚ישׁ מֵיטִ֣יב לְנַגֵּ֔ן וַהֲבִיאוֹתֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Saul to his servants, See, please, for me a man doing well to play, and bring [him] to me.
pieces: So Saul said to his officials, "Find me a man who plays well and bring him to me."

L.17: And Saul said to his servants, "Find, please, for me a man who plays well, and bring [him] to me."

R.17: So Saul told his officials, "Find me someone who plays well and bring him to me."

decisions.choice: see for me: find, look out for me
decisions.reason: "See" in the sense of picking out, as in verse 1, where Yahweh has "seen" a king for himself. Saul now looks for a man for himself, and the one he finds is the one Yahweh has chosen.

decisions.choice: Find
decisions.reason: Literal says "find" here, since "see for me a man" would mislead; the note keeps the link to verse 1.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

records.source: וַיַּעַן֩ אֶחָ֨ד מֵהַנְּעָרִ֜ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה רָאִ֜יתִי בֵּ֣ן לְיִשַׁי֮ בֵּ֣ית הַלַּחְמִי֒ יֹדֵ֣עַ נַ֠גֵּן וְגִבּ֨וֹר חַ֜יִל וְאִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֛ה וּנְב֥וֹן דָּבָ֖ר וְאִ֣ישׁ תֹּ֑אַר וַיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And answered one of the young men and said, Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite knowing playing, and a mighty man of strength, and a man of war, and discerning of word, and a man of form, and Yahweh [is] with him.
pieces: One of the young men replied, "I have seen a son of Jesse in Bethlehem who is a skilled player. He is also a strong warrior and a fighting man. He speaks well, he is handsome, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with him."

L.18: And one of the young men answered and said, "Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play, and [he is] a mighty man of strength and a man of war, and skilled in speech, and a man of [good] form, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with him."

R.18: One of the young men said, "I know a son of Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. He plays the lyre well. He is also brave and strong and knows how to fight. He speaks wisely and is good-looking. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with him."

decisions.choice: Yahweh is with him: the last and weightiest item in the list
decisions.reason: The list ends with the reason behind all the rest. The same is said of David again and again (17:37; 18:12, 14, 28), while of Saul it is said that Yahweh had left him (verse 14; 18:12).

decisions.choice: a mighty man of strength and a man of war: a brave and able fighter
decisions.reason: "Mighty man of strength" is used of a strong warrior (Judges 6:12; 11:1). David is not yet a soldier; the young man may have known of his courage defending the flock against lions and bears (17:34-36). The description looks ahead to his story.

decisions.choice: discerning of word: wise and skilled in speech
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean sensible in what he says or clever in handling matters. Either way, David is no rough shepherd boy.

decisions.choice: a man of form: handsome, of good bearing
decisions.reason: "Form" means shape or figure; it is used of Joseph and Rachel, who were "beautiful of form" (Genesis 29:17; 39:6).

decisions.choice: the young men: Saul's attendants
decisions.reason: These are the servants of verses 15-17, young men who waited on the king.

decisions.choice: [he is]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs to carry the list.

decisions.choice: a strong warrior / brave and strong
decisions.reason: As in Judges 11:1, Balanced says "a strong warrior" for "mighty man of strength"; Readable puts it in plain words.

decisions.choice: I know
decisions.reason: Readable says "I know" for "I have seen": the young man has met David and knows about him.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח שָׁא֛וּל מַלְאָכִ֖ים אֶל־יִשָׁ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁלְחָ֥ה אֵלַ֛י אֶת־דָּוִ֥ד בִּנְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּצֹּֽאן׃
records.gloss: And sent Saul messengers to Jesse and said, Send to me David your son who [is] with the flock.
pieces: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse with the message, "Send me David your son, the one who is with the sheep."

L.19: And Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me David your son, who [is] with the flock."

R.19: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse with this message: "Send me your son David, the one who takes care of the sheep."

decisions.choice: David ... who is with the flock: Saul knows his name and his work
decisions.reason: Saul's servants must have told him more than verse 18 records. "Who is with the flock" echoes Jesse's words in verse 11: the king sends for the shepherd boy whom his own father had not thought to call.

decisions.choice: Saul sends for David
decisions.reason: Without knowing it, the rejected king brings into his own house the one Yahweh has chosen to replace him. The reader knows what Saul does not (verse 13).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח יִשַׁ֜י חֲמ֥וֹר לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְנֹ֣אד יַ֔יִן וּגְדִ֥י עִזִּ֖ים אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח בְּיַד־דָּוִ֥ד בְּנ֖וֹ אֶל־שָׁאֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And took Jesse a donkey [of] bread and a skin of wine and a kid of goats, one, and sent [them] by [the] hand of David his son to Saul.
pieces: So Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, along with a skin of wine and a young goat, and sent them with his son David to Saul.

L.20: And Jesse took a donkey [loaded with] bread, and a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent [them] by the hand of David his son to Saul.

R.20: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread. He added a skin bag full of wine and a young goat. He sent these gifts to Saul with his son David.

decisions.choice: a gift for the king
decisions.reason: A person coming before a king or a man of God brought a gift (9:7-8; 10:27). Jesse sends food from his farm, so that his son comes to Saul with honor.

decisions.choice: a donkey of bread: a donkey loaded with bread
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side, "a donkey, bread", meaning a donkey carrying bread. The same letters could be read as "a homer of bread", a large dry measure, but the plainer reading is the animal, which carried the gifts.

decisions.choice: by the hand of David: with David
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means "through" or "by means of": David takes the gifts.

decisions.choice: a skin bag full of wine ... these gifts
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the wine was carried in an animal skin and calls the goods "gifts" (m1).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֶּאֱהָבֵ֣הֽוּ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיְהִי־ל֖וֹ נֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And came David to Saul and stood before him, and he loved him very much, and he became for him a bearer of weapons.
pieces: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer.

L.21: And David came to Saul and stood before him. And he loved him very much, and he became his weapons bearer.

R.21: David came to Saul and began to serve him. Saul loved David very much, and he made David one of the men who carried his armor and weapons.

decisions.choice: stood before him: entered his service
decisions.reason: To "stand before" a king means to wait on him as a servant (verse 22; 1 Kings 10:8).

decisions.choice: he loved him: Saul loved David
decisions.reason: The verse does not name the subject, but it is Saul, as verse 22 shows. The love of Saul, Jonathan, Michal and all Israel for David runs through the next chapters (18:1, 16, 20), until Saul's love turns to fear and hatred (18:8-12).

decisions.choice: bearer of weapons: armor-bearer
decisions.reason: An armor-bearer carried the weapons and shield of a leader and fought at his side (14:6-14; Judges 9:54). It was a post of trust close to the king; Saul may have had several.

decisions.choice: Saul ... David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people where the Hebrew has only "he" and "him" (m2).

decisions.choice: armor-bearer
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the familiar term; Literal keeps "weapons bearer" and Readable says what the job was, with "one of the men" for the possibility of several (m3).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שָׁא֔וּל אֶל־יִשַׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר יַעֲמָד־נָ֤א דָוִד֙ לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי־מָ֥צָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And sent Saul to Jesse saying, Let stand, please, David before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.
pieces: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, "Please let David stay in my service, for I am very pleased with him."

L.22: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Let David, please, stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes."

R.22: Then Saul sent a message to Jesse: "Please let David stay and serve me. I like him very much."

decisions.choice: let David stand before me: let him stay in my service
decisions.reason: As in verse 21, standing before the king means serving him. Saul asks Jesse to let his son remain at court.

decisions.choice: he has found favor in my eyes: I am pleased with him
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to win his goodwill and approval (Genesis 6:8; Ruth 2:2, 10).

decisions.choice: I am very pleased with him / I like him very much
decisions.reason: The idiom is put in ordinary words (m2); Literal keeps it.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה בִּֽהְי֤וֹת רֽוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וְלָקַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־הַכִּנּ֖וֹר וְנִגֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְרָוַ֤ח לְשָׁאוּל֙ וְט֣וֹב ל֔וֹ וְסָ֥רָה מֵעָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ הָרָעָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And it was, when was a spirit of God to Saul, and took David the lyre and played with his hand, and there was relief for Saul and good [was] for him, and turned aside from on him the spirit of the evil.
pieces: So whenever the spirit from God came on Saul, David would take the lyre and play it. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.

L.23: And it happened, whenever the spirit of God was on Saul, that David took the lyre and played with his hand. And Saul was refreshed, and it was good for him, and the evil spirit turned away from him.

R.23: From then on, whenever the evil spirit from God came on Saul, David would take his lyre and play music. Saul would calm down and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away from him.

decisions.choice: whenever ... would: something that happened again and again
decisions.reason: The verbs describe a pattern repeated over time, not a single event.

decisions.choice: the spirit of God: the evil spirit of verses 14-16
decisions.reason: Here the phrase lacks "evil" at first, but the end of the verse shows that the evil spirit sent from God is meant (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: relief: a play on "spirit"
decisions.reason: The verb for "was relieved", ravach, means to have room to breathe, and sounds like ruach, "spirit" or "breath". When the spirit comes, David's music gives Saul breathing space.

decisions.choice: turned away from him: the words used of the Spirit of Yahweh in verse 14
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 14 returns: the Spirit of Yahweh had turned away from Saul; now the evil spirit turns away when the one on whom the Spirit rests plays for him. The chapter closes with the rejected king soothed by the chosen one, a calm that will not last (18:10-11).

decisions.choice: the spirit from God
decisions.reason: Balanced says "from God" as in verses 15-16, keeping the lowercase "spirit" for the evil spirit as opposed to the Spirit of the LORD.

decisions.choice: the evil spirit from God
